newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai authorities dispute Moody's downgrade move.
newsitem.headline: Thai authorities dispute Moody's downgrade move.

text.p: Thailand on Wednesday disputed Moody's decision to downgrade the country's long-term foreign currency debt ceiling ratings and said the agency failed to take into account measures launched to solve economic problems.

"I'm not saying that they were wrong. But I do wish though that they would give more weight to the government's determination in solving problems," Bank of Thailand assistant governor Siri Ganjareondee told Reuters.
"Thailand should be assessed for its dynamic picture and not the static one," he said.
Siri added that Thailand had some problems with the proportion of its short-term debt, inconsistencies between currency and interest rate policy and its financial and property sector.
"But the authorities have done whatever is needed to be done to address these problems. But it will take time before the results show," he said.
Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday it has downgraded the foreign currency ceiling for bonds and bank deposits of Thailand to A3 from A2.

Moody's said the erosion of the country's creditworthiness was caused by a build-up of short-term foreign debt, structural problems that affected Thai competitiveness, constraints on the range and effectiveness of macroeconomic policies, and the crisis in the domestic financial and property sector.
